bang3.title: Rohingya genocide case to proceed
bang3.description: The World Court yesterday rejected Myanmar’s objections to a genocide case over its treatment of the Muslim Rohingya minority, paving the way for the case to be heard in full.

bang3.title: Need 1 week to assess situation
bang3.description: Admitting that the Power Division could not impose schedule-wise power cuts across the country, State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Nasrul Hamid yesterday sought one week’s time to address the issue.

bang3.title: Wasfia 1st Bangladeshi to conquer K2
bang3.description: Renowned Bangladeshi mountaineer Wasfia Nazreen conquered the treacherous K2 in Pakistan, becoming the first person from Bangladesh to summit the second-tallest mountain in the world.

bang3.title: CU sexual assault: Fingers pointed at BCL men
bang3.description: Those who sexually assaulted a female student on Chittagong University campus on July 17 night are members of Bangladesh Chhatra League, said police sources and CU BCL insiders.

bang3.title: Noab hikes newspaper price by Tk 2 from Jul 25
bang3.description: All newspapers owned by the members of Newspaper Owners’ Association of Bangladesh (Noab) will see a price increase of at least Tk 2 per issue from July 25.

bang3.title: Yet-to-start mega projects: Consider putting  them on hold
bang3.description: Given the current economic situation, the government should consider suspending mega projects the physical work of which has yet to begin, economist Debapriya Bhattacharya said yesterday.

bang3.title: ‘You cannot remain silent’
bang3.description: The High Court yesterday came down hard on Bangladesh Railway for mismanagement, ticket scalping and carrying passengers on the train roofs.

bang3.title: Electricity crisis may worsen
bang3.description: The government’s plan for one to two hours of daily power cuts is failing, especially in the north, and the signs are that the electricity crisis may worsen across the country in the coming days.

bang3.title: EC’s dialogue hits a snag as BNP skips it
bang3.description: The BNP yesterday skipped Election Commission’s dialogue seeking recommendations of political parties on how to hold a free and fair general election.

ca3.title: Insurance covered the rebuild of her house after a fire. Why didn’t the bank release the money on time?
ca3.description: Georgetown, Ont., property owner Antonina Gladkova is warning others to pay attention to their mortgage agreements after her lender didn't dole out insurance payments on pace with her contractor's invoices, leaving her on the hook to cover costly shortfalls to rebuild her property after a fire.

ca3.title: 'To avoid scandal': Unearthed letters show how N.L. bishop handled allegations in Baie Verte
ca3.description: A new court action in Grand Falls-Windsor has unearthed letters showing how a Catholic church official moved a priest to an Ontario treatment centre following allegations involving boys in 1970 — more than 15 years before he was convicted of sexual assault.

ca3.title: Food and shelter have driven Canada's affordability crisis. Health care isn't far behind
ca3.description: Food and shelter grab headlines, but out-of-pocket health-care expenses have climbed at a nearly identical rate since 2022, Statistics Canada data shows. Economists and policy experts break down the structural drivers behind Canada's rising private medical costs.

ca3.title: Blue Jays pitcher Dylan Cease launches artwork, retail collection at Art Gallery of Ontario
ca3.description: The collection includes prints, postcards and totes, with proceeds going to support the gallery's charitable mission.

ca3.title: B.C. real estate agent fined $200K, suspended after buying and renting out affordable housing unit
ca3.description: A Victoria real estate agent has been fined $200,000 and had his licence suspended for six months after he bought an affordable housing unit and rented it out, according to a consent order posted by the B.C. Financial Services Authority.

ca3.title: Loblaw backtracks on dropping country-of-origin produce labels after customer backlash
ca3.description: Loblaw has reversed course on its decision earlier this month to drop country-of-origin labeling on produce signs in its stores in most provinces, following customer backlash.

ca3.title: FOI reveals operator of Sandman Hotel chain fined over $620K for asbestos violations
ca3.description: In the report — which details the $624,051.48 penalty handed to Northland Properties — B.C.'s workplace regulator says the company failed to ensure workers were safe when they worked on a renovation project at the Williams Lake hotel in December 2025.

ca3.title: Canada's big banks are shrugging off Trump's trade war
ca3.description: Top executives at the Bank of Montreal and Scotiabank separately referred to the Canada-U.S. trade situation as "manageable" on Tuesday.

ca3.title: Edmonton Pride Festival says it needed to work with police after receiving bomb threat
ca3.description: The Edmonton Pride Festival says it stands by the level of police presence it had at this year’s Pride parade, revealing it received a bomb threat leading up to the event.

ca3.title: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith wants Ottawa to resume trade talks with U.S. before counter-tariffs begin
Premiers told to 'bridge past' Trump administration amid tariff war, Manitoba's Wab Kinew says
ca3.description: Conversations with Mark Carney amid an escalating U.S. trade war have focused on the long haul, with the prime minister telling premiers to prepare economic programs to "bridge past the Trump administration," says Wab Kinew.

ca3.title: Venue cancels anti-immigration group's conference booking in Hamilton, police say
ca3.description: Hamilton police say a venue that had rented space to an anti-immigration group for its national conference later this week has cancelled the booking. This follows weeks of community groups, politicians and experts condemning Dominion Society of Canada.

ca3.title: Passenger recounts moment plane fatally struck Montreal airport ground worker
ca3.description: An employee at Montreal's Trudeau International Airport has died after he was struck by a plane on Monday evening. The victim was 39-year-old Oscar Robayo, according to his union.

ca3.title: Trump tariffs force iconic Montreal deli to ditch soda staple for locally-made cola
ca3.description: While the smoked meat sandwich is what made Schwartz's Deli arguably Montreal's most famous restaurant, regulars know the traditional refreshment to grab with that order is a can of Cott's black cherry soda — a can the restaurant can no longer obtain due to new tariffs.

ca3.title: Toronto rapper gets life in prison, no parole for at least 22 years in double murder at Fort Erie, Ont., party
ca3.description: A Toronto rapper convicted of two counts of second-degree murder in the shootings of two young women at a Fort Erie, Ont., house party will spend 22 years in prison before he's eligible for parole. Christine Crooks of Toronto and Juliana Pannunzio of Windsor were killed in January 2021.

ca3.title: Blue Jays pitcher Bieber out with shoulder injury in midst of playoff push
ca3.description: The Toronto Blue Jays have placed right-handed pitcher Shane Bieber on the 15-day injured list with inflammation of his right teres major muscle.

ca3.title: First Nations businesses, communities brace for Canada-U.S. trade war
ca3.description: First Nations are grappling with uncertainty and bracing for impact as the Canada-U.S. trade war escalates, with steep tariffs taking effect on some business sectors.

ca3.title: N.L. premier reaching out to 'key industry partners' as trade war ramps up
ca3.description: N.L. political leaders are commenting on the latest in the Canada-U.S. trade dispute.

ca3.title: Former Alberta premier Jason Kenney calls on province to take tougher approach to U.S. trade war
ca3.description: Speaking on CBC Radio's Calgary Eyeopener Tuesday morning, the former United Conservative Party leader said export taxes on the province's energy resources should be on the table to put additional pressure on U.S. President Donald Trump.

ca3.title: What would help health care in the N.W.T.'s Dehcho? Residents say it’s about relationships
ca3.description: A recent set of recommendations on improving health care in the region focuses on staffing and equipment but what matters most, some residents say, is relationships. The recommendations follow a months-long investigation into the deaths of three Dehcho residents in early 2025.
